Subject: Unexpected p95/p99 spike on embeddings endpoint after catalog promotion

Marissa,

We started seeing significant latency regressions on our embeddings calls around 23:35 UTC on 2027-03-14, right after you pushed the model catalog promotion. Baseline p95 for our workload was ~120ms; it jumped to ~640ms and p99s are hitting 2.1s intermittently. Error rates are low (~0.2%) but timeouts and client-side retries are spiking which is impacting throughput.

We run steady batches of 16 upserts and synchronous queries against /v1/embeddings. The only change on our side was the model selector to the new recommended variant (model: embed-bison-1q-v2).

We attached traces and a small CSV with p95/p99 snapshots and a compressed trace bundle. Can you triage? This is affecting our nightly ingestion window and the data science team is blocked.

Attachments:
- helio_traces_20270315.json.gz (trace spans, 30MB compressed)
- p95_p99_snapshot_20270315.csv

Ravi / team — quick update from the SRE side after initial triage:
- We confirmed the catalog promotion at 2027-03-14T23:31:12Z (promote manifest attached).
- Regression is localized to the quantized execution path for embed-bison-1q-v2 on our A100-optimized runtime. CPU side scheduling is normal; the GPU kernel time is up ~4-6x for several op kernels used by that variant (attention + rotary interleave).
- Canary coverage was 2% globally; HelioSearch landed on the promoted variant during their steady traffic window.

Immediate remediation actions taken:
1) Applied a traffic override for HelioSearch to pin them to embed-bison-1q-v1 (previous variant) at 17:20 PST. This should bring p95s back down within the next 10-15 minutes.
2) Opened internal issue INC-2027-314.
3) Engaging runtime team to look at kernel/graph differences; possibility of a regression in fused kernel selection when sequence-length < 128 + batch 16 pattern.

Ravi — can you confirm if you see latency improving after the pin? We will follow with a full RCA.

Attachments: catalog_promo_manifest_20270314.json

Ben Carter
Sr Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@heliosearch.com>, finance@heliosearch.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Exec update: HelioSearch embeddings latency — mitigation and next steps

Ravi — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Quick executive summary and actions: 

1) Root cause (preliminary): a change in the promoted model variant (embed-bison-1q-v2) caused the runtime to pick an alternate fused kernel path for certain short-sequence batches (typical for HelioSearch). That kernel path exhibits higher tail latency on our A100 profile; this appears to be a performance regression introduced during quantization tuning for v2.

2) Mitigation performed: Ben applied a traffic override at 2027-03-16T17:20:00-07:00 to return HelioSearch to embed-bison-1q-v1. We observed p95 drop from ~640ms -> ~140ms within 12 minutes and p99 tail normalize.

3) Next steps (timeline):
- Today: keep traffic override for HelioSearch and monitor for 72 hours.
- 48 hours: runtime team will produce a kernel-level patch or adjust the kernel selection heuristic; if patch not ready, we will hold the catalog promotion for global rollout until validation completes.
- 5 business days: full RCA and customer-facing postmortem with timelines for permanent fix.

4) Remediation offer: we will apply a one-time service credit to HelioSearch for the impacted ingestion window (details via finance).

Links:
- Incident page: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2027-314-helio-vec
- RCA draft (internal): https://drive.redwood/helio/rca-draft-2027-03-18

Marissa will follow up with a formal postmortem and attach the final logs. Im available if you want to escalate to a higher SLA or discuss Dedicated capacity options to reduce single-variant exposure.

Regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Success & Reliability
Redwood Inference
